subtitle: The Liskov Substitution Principle states that when there is a parent object and a child object that inherits from it, the child object must be able to completely substitute for the parent object in any operation that calls the parent object. In object-oriented languages, inheritance occurs between objects. Through this process, a parent/child relationship is defined. A child object inherits the characteristics of its parent object and can extend upon them. However, in this process, overreaching or extensions that stray from the intent of the object can lead to improper inheritance. The Liskov Substitution Principle recommends that, for proper inheritance, a child object's extension should fully follow the direction of the parent object.
